claims.question: q1
claims.claim: In the initial feature task, using an AI assistant yielded a 30.7% median reduction in completion time, and habitual AI users showed an estimated 55.9% speedup.
claims.quote: Observational results from Phase 1 corroborate prior research: using an AI assistant yielded a 30.7% median reduction in completion time, and habitual AI users showed an estimated 55.9% speedup.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: In the downstream randomized trial, evolving AI-co-developed solutions without AI assistance showed no significant differences in completion time or code quality.
claims.quote: Phase 2 revealed no significant differences in subsequent evolution with respect to completion time or code quality.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Bayesian analysis found that any speed or quality improvements from AI use were at most small and highly uncertain.
claims.quote: Bayesian analysis suggests that any speed or quality improvements from AI use were at most small and highly uncertain.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The study did not detect systematic maintainability advantages or disadvantages when other developers evolved code co-developed with AI assistants.
claims.quote: Overall, we did not detect systematic maintainability advantages or disadvantages when other developers evolved code co-developed with AI assistants.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: Within the study's tasks and measures, there were no consistent warning signs of degraded code-level maintainability.
claims.quote: Within the scope of our tasks and measures, we observed no consistent warning signs of degraded code-level maintainability.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The two-phase controlled experiment involved 151 participants, 95% of whom were professional developers.
claims.quote: We conducted a two-phase controlled experiment involving 151 participants, 95% of whom were professional developers.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The authors say future work should examine risks such as code bloat from excessive code generation and cognitive debt from offloading mental effort to assistants.
claims.quote: Future work should examine risks such as code bloat from excessive code generation and cognitive debt as developers offload more mental effort to assistants.
